reason: Umbelliform describes inflorescence form. A tree crown or a fruit can also be umbrella-shaped, and that is a different meaning.
Polymorphic means variable in form. PATO variant shape means a shape that differs from the normal one. The rule loses the 'varies between forms' meaning, so it is better not mapped.
Baccate means berry-like, so fleshy fits fruit. It does not fit other parts.
A suckering plant produces sucker shoots. PO lists sucker as a synonym of root-borne shoot system.
Gaping means standing open, as in a gaping corolla or calyx. PATO open fits.
This is the plain negation of constricted.
Lineate means marked with fine lines. Striated is the closest PATO term.
Trigonal and trigonous both mean three-angled in cross-section.
Eccentric means off-centre, so 'not centered' fits.
Horny means hard, like horn, as in horny endosperm or horny texture.
Stony means hard as stone, as in a stony endocarp.
Toothless means without teeth, so not dentated fits.
Included means not protruding, which is the opposite of exserted, so it applies to stamens, styles and similar parts. 'Enclosed' on other parts, such as a seed in a fruit, only describes containment.
Grouped means clustered, so aggregated fits.
Nervate means having nerves or veins. PO lists vein as a synonym of vascular bundle.
Metallic means a metal-like sheen, often with colour such as metallic blue. Glistening loses the metal-like part.
Reticulately veined means a net-like vein pattern, so reticulate fits.
Already limited to the whole plant or habit, where low-growing means decreased height.
Rosette means arranged in a rosette, so rosulate fits.
Trichotomous means divided into three, so tripartite fits.
Paleaceous means chaffy or bearing paleae (scales). Scarious means thin, dry and membranous. They overlap but are not the same, so the rule loses the 'bearing chaff scales' meaning.
Homogeneous endosperm means not ruminate. The rule is limited to endosperm and seed.
Not raised means not prominent.
Flanged means having a flange or rim. A wing is a broader, flatter outgrowth, so the rule loses the 'rim' meaning.
Stiped means having a stipe, which is stipitate.
Floriferous means bearing flowers.
This is the plain negation of winged.
PO uses awn for grass spikelet parts. A bristle-tipped leaf or phyllary has a bristle or mucro, not an awn.
Copious means abundant, so increased amount fits.
An imperfect flower lacks stamens or pistils, which is unisexual. The rule is limited to flower, floret and inflorescence.
Eroded means a margin that looks gnawed, which is erose.
Polished means a glossy surface.
Ephemeral means short-lived, as in flowers or plants.
This is the plain negation of swollen.
Cohering means sticking together, which is coherent.
Scarcely visible means inconspicuous.
Subapical means just below the tip, which is subterminal.
Head-like means capitate.
Pink-tinged means with a pink tint. It is the usual mapping for 'tinged', though the pink is faint.
Tongue-shaped (ligulate or lingulate) is close to strap-shaped.
Erecto-patent means between erect and spreading, which is close to ascending.

target: PATO_0001325 radial symmetry (or PATO_0001328 actinomorphic, for flowers)
reason: In descriptions, radial usually means radial symmetry. Radiating means spreading out from a centre, which is a different thing.
Involucrate means having an involucre.
Infundibular means funnel-shaped.
An undershrub is a subshrub, which is suffrutescent.
Excavate means hollowed out, so concave fits.
Tap, as in tap root, is PO primary root (tap root is its synonym).
Scarce means few, so decreased amount fits.
Digitately compound is the same as digitate, which means palmately compound.
Pithy means containing pith in stems. For fruit, 'pithy' means a spongy flesh, which is not the pith.
